decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build directly on the firm's core drilling, bonding and polishing know-how, so it can interpret customer feedback and keep improving the product through its own R&D.
Carrier wafers for smaller diameters are a close extension of its established carrier and thin-wafer handling expertise and fit its strategic push toward reusable carriers.

The Cu-interposer is a flagship that rests on the firm's glass structuring and through-via competence, and its R&D and EU project experience give it the absorptive capacity to develop the technology further.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand packages the firm's core standard glass and quartz wafers, needs little new knowledge, and broadens market reach at low risk.

Glass-based circuit boards lie far from the firm's wafer-level knowledge base and narrow product focus, so it has limited capacity to assimilate PCB-market knowledge, and the resources are better redirected to its core substrate and interposer development.
